entries.reason: a plain three-float struct constructor with no OS dependency: the caller only ever constructs and compares the value, and rank 121 of the crash-demand table is a LOAD-FAIL on this exact symbol for provenance - a hard, non-weak import that kills the application at launch if it is not carried
entries.effect: returns {minimum, maximum, preferred} exactly as given, the header's own definition

entries.reason: the struct's own field-by-field equality, carried alongside CAFrameRateRangeMake() rather than left as a second gap beside the one that crashes
entries.effect: true when minimum, maximum and preferred are each equal, false otherwise

entries.reason: the sentinel value the header documents for "no preference", carried as a real exported constant rather than a NULL weak reference
entries.effect: {-1, -1, -1}, the value Apple's own documentation gives for CAFrameRateRange.default
entries.source: SDK 16.4, QuartzCore/CAFrameRateRange.h; Apple's public documentation of CAFrameRateRange.default

entries.reason: CAAnimation carries no display link of its own to throttle - kept and returned faithfully rather than declared absent, the same way this port already keeps a property it cannot act on elsewhere
entries.effect: stores and returns the exact range given, starting at CAFrameRateRangeDefault; never messaged further, since CoreAnimation on this release commits at the one rhythm the render server drives and a real device with no ProMotion display answers this property the same way

entries.reason: the header deprecates preferredFramesPerSecond (already carried, ios10framerate.json) in favor of this property, so it drives the same frameInterval mechanism rather than being a second, disconnected store
entries.effect: stores the exact range given and drives preferredFramesPerSecond from preferred (or maximum, if preferred is unset), clamped to [minimum, maximum] when both are given; reads back the exact range last set, or CAFrameRateRangeDefault
